drills.q: Name the two computational primitives that every RAGAS/DeepEval metric reduces to.
drills.a: Claim decomposition plus judge verdict (faithfulness, context recall), and reverse-question generation plus embedding similarity (answer relevancy).

drills.q: A faithfulness score of 1.0 comes back on an answer you suspect is wrong. What's the first thing to check?
drills.a: Whether the retrieved context itself is correct -- faithfulness only checks the answer against retrieved context, never against the world, so a faithful answer grounded in a wrong chunk scores 1.0.

drills.q: Roughly how many LLM calls does a single faithfulness computation cost, and why?
drills.a: About 4-7 calls: 1 to decompose the answer into 3-6 atomic claims, plus 1 per claim to check support against context.

drills.q: Your team wants to run RAGAS, DeepEval, and LangSmith evals in parallel on every PR 'for redundancy.' Push back on this.
drills.a: All three implement close variants of the same claim-decomposition judge primitive, so this roughly triples judge-call cost and CI time for correlated noise, not three independent signals. Pick one calibrated source of truth per metric family instead.

drills.q: Faithfulness moved from 0.82 to 0.77 after a prompt change on a 300-row eval set. Is this a real regression? What do you do before concluding either way?
drills.a: Not necessarily -- continuous judge scores have rerun noise (~14% flip rate on comparisons) and bootstrap CI half-widths of ~3-5pp. Run a paired difference test on the same examples before/after rather than comparing raw means before concluding it's real.

drills.q: Design a sample-size argument for how many paired examples you need to trust a 5-point faithfulness delta as real.
drills.a: Using n ~ 2*sigma^2*(z_alpha/2+z_beta)^2/delta^2 with sigma~0.15-0.25 and delta=0.05, you land around 100-250 paired examples at 80% power and alpha=0.05 -- below that, a 3-5pt swing is indistinguishable from noise.

drills.q: Explain what DeepEval's assert_test() is doing mechanically, and why it makes your test suite inherently flakier than a normal pytest suite.
drills.a: It's a normal pytest assertion, but the value under test is a continuous score from a noisy LLM judge call rather than a deterministic computation -- so thresholds need headroom above the metric's known noise floor, and single-run failures shouldn't be treated as proof of a regression.

drills.q: A teammate proposes using Promptfoo's llm-rubric assertion as the sole quality gate for a RAG feature. What's the specific gap?
drills.a: llm-rubric doesn't decompose retrieval from generation the way RAGAS/DeepEval's four metrics do, so you lose the attribution table that tells you whether a regression is a retrieval problem or a generation problem.

drills.q: Your nightly RAGAS suite costs $40/night with a frontier judge. Leadership wants it cut to $10 without losing the ability to catch real regressions. Design the fix.
drills.a: Route the bulk of examples to a cheap judge, escalate only borderline/near-threshold scores to the frontier judge for adjudication (cheap/frontier router pattern), and batch per-claim verdict checks into fewer calls where structured output supports it. Recalibrate against human labels specifically for the cheap judge before trusting its absolute numbers.

drills.q: After upgrading DeepEval to a new minor version, your faithfulness scores shift by 6 points overnight with no code or prompt change. Diagnose and fix the process gap.
drills.a: The framework's default metric prompt or judge model likely changed silently between versions with no changelog entry read. Treat any framework version upgrade like a judge-model swap: pin versions explicitly, and re-run human-label calibration before trusting post-upgrade scores.

drills.q: A stakeholder sees a 95% pass rate on your DeepEval suite and wants to ship, but support tickets are rising. What's missing from the suite that would explain this gap?
drills.a: The suite's canned metric rubrics were likely never calibrated against human labels for this product's actual definition of quality, and/or the golden set has gone stale relative to current production traffic -- a passing suite only means the system agrees with an uncalibrated judge's opinion of itself.
